content:
Amazon now officially announced its Black Friday sale and launched its early Black Friday event alongside the ongoing Apple HomeView pre-order deal and AirPods Pro 3 at $50 off. You’ll want to go secure yourself (and some stockings) 2026 Apple Polishing Cloths at $9 Prime shipped, but we are now tracking additional M5 MacBook Air models at $250 off as well as some official Apple refurb configs at $300 off. Those deals join Apple Watch Ultra 4 at nearly $100 off as well as the early Black Friday deals on Apple’s latest M6 Mac mini lineup at up to $150 off and these Amazon all-time lows on Apple’s Magic Trackpad in white and black. We have Twelve South’s adjustable metal Curve Mini stand for your OLED iPad mini and/or iPhone Duo down at $40, the popular Airfly Drive CarPlay wireless adapter back in-stock, and loads more accessory deals waiting below.

Stocking stuffer alert: 2026 Apple Polishing Cloth back in-stock at $9 Prime shipped

AirPods Pro 3 $50 off, AirPods Max 2 $100 off in early Black Friday sales launching today

  • AirPods Pro 3 $199 (Reg. $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 $449 (Reg. $549)

Amazon’s pre-order discount on the new Apple HomeView is back

Amazon’s pre-order discount on the new Apple HomeView has returned once again today. While shipping at times at Apple have gotten better on some models, Amazon is now selling it for less and delivering quicker to some regions of the country.

M5 MacBook Air 24GB now $250 off new, or $300 off via Apple refurb store

The M5 MacBook Air 1TB configs down at $250 off, including both the 13-inch and 15-inch models, have thus far been some of the most notable early Black Friday deals. Those deals are still live alongside the most affordable model at $1,099 ($200 off), but we also just spotted this 24GB variant at nearly $250 off as well.

Amazon is still offering both the 13- and 15-inch 16GB/1TB M5 MacBook Air configurations at $250 off the list price for what is easily the best deal in new condition in over 4 months.

However, the remainder of the models were sitting at $200 off until this 24GB/1TB config with the 15-inch display dropped to $1,749.99 – that’s $249 off the regular $1,999 list price. Still much more pricey than the previously mentioned options, and only in Sky Blue as of right now, but also the lowest price in a long time.

  • 13-inch M5 MacBook Air 16GB/512GB $1,099 (Reg. $1,299)
  • 13-inch M5 MacBook Air 16GB/1TB $1,349 (Reg. $1,599) – $250 off
  • 13-inch M5 MacBook Air 24GB/1TB $1,599 (Reg. $1,799)
  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air 16GB/512GB $1,299 (Reg. $1,499)
  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air 16GB/1TB $1,549 (Reg. $1,799) – $250 off
  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air 24GB/1TB from $1,749 (Reg. $1,999) – $250 off

We would remiss not to at least mention this 15-inch 24GB/1TB model’s listing on the official Apple Refurbished Store – it is now $300 off at $1,699 shipped with a full Apple warranty. That is only $50 less than the price we are targeting for Black Friday this year on brand new units, but it will, nonetheless, save you some cash:

  • 15-inch M5 MacBook Air 24GB/1TB from $1,699 (Reg. $1,999 new) – $300 off
  • Midnight, Silver, and Starlight

Apple’s Magic Trackpad now sitting at Amazon all-time low pricing

There are plenty of folks out there that transform their MacBook setup at home into a docketed situation with an external mouse, keyboard, and even a separate Trackpad, ourselves included. And with the new current M5 MacBook Air down to the best prices in months at up to $250 off right now, and the new M6 MacBook Pro and touch display model now out in the wild, we wanted to highlight these relatively rare all-time lows on Apple’s Magic Trackpad in white and black.

Deals on Apple’s Magic Trackpad are incredibly rare. And while we have started to see the prices drop slowly on the latest black and white models over the last few months, we wanted to make sure the current all-time low pricing at Amazon was on the radar for folks looking to upgrade their setup:

  • Apple Magic Trackpad White $116 (Reg. $129)
  • Apple Magic Trackpad Black $130 (Reg. $149)

We clearly aren’t looking at massive deals here on Apple’s multi-touch surface, but, again, that’s not really a thing with Magic Trackpad. Deals on most Magic accessories are rare, and the perhaps most of all on Trackpad. While both models have very slowly dropped in price across 2026, they are now sitting at Amazon all-time lows and it’s hard to say if they will be any more deals for Black Friday or not – we didn’t see any additional savings on either of them last year.

Be sure to scope out our recent feature on the best MacBook Pro accessories to elevate your setup right here.

M6 Mac mini early Black Friday deals now live at up to $150 off

Amazon officially announced its upcoming Black Friday sale and launched its early Black Friday sale pages today loaded with deals. These offers also sit alongside M5 MacBook Air at up to $250 off as well as the ongoing all-time lows on Apple’s latest M6 Mac mini lineup at up to $150 off.

Early Black Friday M6 Mac mini deals

  • M6 Mac mini 16GB/256GB $779 (Reg. $899)
  • M6 Mac mini 16GB/512GB $949 (Reg. $1,099)
  • M6 Mac mini 24GB/512GB $1,149 (Reg. $1,299)
  • M5 Pro Mac mini 24GB/512GB $1,549 (Reg. $1,699)

As you can see above, Amazon’s particularly notable $150 price drops are still rolling on the upgraded M6 Mac mini and the more powerful M5 Pro config, as well as the $120 discount on the most affordable model in the lineup.

Save for a slightly lower dip on the entry model at about $10 less, you’re looking at deals on par with the lowest we have tracked, all of which popped up as part of the fall Prime Day event.

As we push closer to the start of Amazon’s official Black Friday sale, it remains unclear whether or not the latest M6 Mac mini lineup will drop any lower than we are tracking right now. They are, after all, brand new releases and anything more than this would be particularly amazing. While a $200 discount is not out of the question here, landing the 2026 mini in and around $150 off is still a wonderful discount and a great way to upgrade your setup with Apple’s newest chips.
